english: For each positive integer $n$, let $S_{n}=\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{n}2^{k}\cos\dfrac{k\pi}{3}$. Then the greatest value of $S_{n}$ for $1\leq n\leq10$ is ______.
hindi: प्रत्येक धनात्मक पूर्णांक $n$ के लिए माना कि $S_{n}=\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{n}2^{k}\cos\dfrac{k\pi}{3}$ है। तब $1\leq n\leq10$ के लिए $S_{n}$ का महत्तम मान ______ है।
solution: For $1\leq n\leq10$ the positive values are $S_{1}=1$, $S_{6}=63$, $S_{7}=127$; greatest $=127$
solution_full: Let $u=2\left(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{3}+i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)=1+i\sqrt{3}$. By De Moivre's theorem, $u^{k}=2^{k}\left(\cos\dfrac{k\pi}{3}+i\sin\dfrac{k\pi}{3}\right)$, so $S_{n}=\mathrm{Re}\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{n}u^{k}$.
The angles $\dfrac{k\pi}{3}$ are in AP, so the series is a GP in $u$: $\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{n}u^{k}=\dfrac{u(u^{n}-1)}{u-1}$ ($u\neq1$).
originality_note: New: a geometrically weighted cosine series with angles in AP whose partial sums, via De Moivre, collapse to 2^n - 1, -1 or -2^n - 1 according to n mod 6, and the question asks for the largest partial sum (way 2, a sequence analysed after a construction). Closest known: sum of r^k cos k theta (infinite GP) and sum of cos k theta in AP. Different because: r = 2 > 1, so the partial sums oscillate wildly and the maximum over a range must be found from the mod-6 pattern.
blueprint_concepts: Summation of trigonometric series with angles in AP

concept_use.De Moivre theorem: u^k = 2^k e^{i k pi/3} turns the cosine series into the real part of a GP in u = 1 + i sqrt3.
concept_use.Summation of trigonometric series with a: The angles k pi/3 are in AP; the GP sum gives the closed form 2^{n+1}/sqrt3 sin((n+1)pi/3) - 1, whose periodic pattern is used.

key_step: Sum the GP in u = 1 + i sqrt3, simplify u/(u-1) = 1 - i/sqrt3, and read S_n by n mod 6.
justification: De Moivre GP summation plus a compound-angle reduction and a periodic case split; numerical with no options. Average Advanced, near 2025-P2-Q13 (L4) but with a more standard route, so 3.
